I have played the pirated version of it, a decade ago.Bought this just to support them, It was 10/10 at that time, it is still 10/10 but we cant play it because they have bricked it or it is broken and doesnt play well on modern PC. 
So, may be dont buy it, wait for the reboot/remake which is in works.
Unable to play it in full screen, doesnt support ultrawide resolutions. They updated it last in 2024 and we now know that they are remaking this game and this game is bricked now. One can only play this in widnowed mode on modern PCs, at a max 1080p ratio, else it just shows black screen. Earlier it was phones who use to brick or slow the phones with an update just before releasing a newer phone, may be game studios are learning from them...

Still holds up as a fun game today and if it crashes on startup there is a mod on Nexus Mods called Fallout 3 Intel bypass package and trust me its worth it.

Why is this game still available for purchase when it's literally unplayable from Windows 10 and up? I got it to work after modding it, only to realise the quests, radio and entire game in general was broken from the inside. 

Thank GOD for the Tale of Two Wastelands mod and its creators, it literally imports Fallout 3 onto the Fallout New Vegas engine, which still works, making this game playable again. So, for anyone wanting to purchase it, I greatly recommend just buying Fallout New Vegas too, just to install the Tale of Two Wastelands mod.

Won't start up after pressing new game. Apparently I am not the only one with this issue. Looked for fixes but haven't worked for me so far. Even if I find a fix I will rate this game negatively because Bethesda should have fixed this bug ages ago. It should NOT be for sale if the game doesn't work without a mod for it to simply run. Should be against steam's TOS for games to be unable to be launched as well but greed and corporations go hand in hand.

Edit: I have got the game working through a fix on Nexus mods, my point still stands about Bethesda not fixing this game anyway.

I genuinely do not understand how anyone can call this their favorite entry in the series. You literally cannot even launch the game without installing mods because it is so fundamentally broken. Once you actually get it running, the story is just completely awful and stupid. The combat is incredibly frustrating because even the most powerful weapons in the game feel like they do barely any damage to basic enemies. It gets old so fast that I eventually just gave up and downloaded a teleport mod to get around. Even though I got this on discount, I still desperately wish I could refund this mistake of a game. Paying anything at all for this piece of garbage feels like a waste. Honestly, I've seen mobile games with better design than this crap. -1/10, do not buy this unless you want to be heavily annoyed and disappointed.

It crashed on the bootup menu. Not even initialized. Not even ingame. 10/10. It just works. Play it with an unofficial patch unless dreaming about playing this game past the first start up is in your cards.

citations.review_text: The game is incredibly detailed storywise, gameplay-wise it is nothing like the first two games, and that is a great thing, exploring can be really slow, so I recommend using a running faster mod; and there is a ton of bugs, some patch mod to fix the bugs is also recommended.

It's still one of the best games of the early 2000s. 

The gameplay holds up somewhat, ageing like a tasty cheese instead of a fine wine. The graphics brings a wave of welcomed nostalgia. 

The atmosphere is superb, although it lacks the sheer amount of random encounters compared to more recent titles. It still has a lot of unmarked and interesting things you could find by exploring the world. 

And of course, the writing is still above average. Not the best, but certainly above the slop of the modern gaming scene. 

Overall, gameplay is still a solid 7.5/10


Now, here's the downside. The PC port of this diamond in the rough leaves a lot to be desired. So far, I've experienced multiple crashes, with the launcher crashing on start up as well. 

anything disconnecting (I.e controller, bluetooth earphones/mouse/keyboard) would crash the game most definitely. 

Overall, it's a minor inconvenience at best, I lose 2 hours of gameplay at worst.  BUT, this is a game that I would still recommend and actively endorse to be experienced at least once, especially at the price that I got the GOTY version for. 


NOTE: For modern gamers wanting to experience a piece of the Golden age of gaming, keep in mind that this game lacks the modern quality of life features that most games usually have now. 

One of these features is interval auto saving (Autosave every 5 mins), in this game, auto save will only happen if you trigger a loading screen (Going through doors). so SAVE OFTEN, unless you want to lose 1 hours of exploration gameplay.

But beyond that, the experience is unforgettable.If you’re looking for a post apocalyptic adventure with a captivating story, amazing music, and phenomenal atmosphere, Fallout 3 is absolutely worth playing.

Oblivion with guns is what it says on the box, it's oblivion with guns. A famous actor yaps at you for a bit, dips from the plot and shows back up for a bit and dies. citations.review_text:
I played fallout 3 completely for the first time about a year ago. And it was kind of awful but also surprisingly enjoyable at times. When you consider this in the legacy of a game franchise with 3 of the best RPG's of all time in it, it's an abomination that should be scorched from the earth. So we won't be doing that.

Oblivion with guns is what it says on the box, it's oblivion with guns. A famous actor yaps at you for a bit, dips from the plot and shows back up for a bit and dies. Wild changes from it's source material I know. Unfortunately that's about all the postive I can say for the main story. It doesn't make any sense when thought about with the slightest scrutiny, it doesn't involve any of your actions through out the rest of the game and half of it can be circumnavigated by simply walking in the correct direction for doing which, you miss nothing but some of the most boring quests in the game that are not worth doing to begin with. A superior game would use this time finding famous person voice actor to direct you towards worth doing quests but instead the best side quests in this game are seemingly randomly placed out of the way and with no indication of how to get to them. Needless to say the world design could use some work.

But there are good quests and some of the dlc even breaches into the realm of being genuinely good across the board. Moira is obviously one if you look into any of the people talking about side quests Moira's wasteland survival guide is high point and for good reason. It's an actually good quest that sends you out to places with usually other interesting stuff going on, it's almost like it should have been the main quest instead of the actual main quest. You also get charming and witty dialogue options as well as Moira herself being quite the charmer which is rare but a pleasant surprise in this game. Another one is the comic book heroes who are terrorizing a town with their stupid antics and it's up to the player to help them so…

This review would have been positive until the ending happened and I realized what Fallout 3 actually was, the great game of watching NPC's do cool things. It felt like I was being forced into the back seat of what should have been the player character's story. The entire game is an errands simulator and fetch quest machine. The aesthetics and visual design are great, but the main story is just a slog to get through. I truly can't think of a single time when I was forced to make a meaningful or interesting decision that would have impacted the main quest. The Karma system is dated and is simply a way for the devs to say "you picked the bad choice" or "you picked the good choice." not to mention the combat is easy and lacks imagination. Fallout 1 and 2 forced the player to actually think about how the player's build would interact with combat and play to their strengths, sometimes avoiding combat entirely. Where on the other had, fallout 3 seams to just reward the play with crazy damage by using a weapon of a type that the player just put skill points into, effectively trivialising combat, on top of that I felt like so many skills were just irrelevant, to be fair this is a criticism I have with the previous two games in the franchise but when the main combat is dull and the main story is un-interesting and un-engaging, it sends the last nail in an already tightly closed coffin.

Fallout 3 is a good example of how not to make a Fallout game. Few of your choices matter, the worldbuilding is broken as hell, the gameplay is mediocre, and the writing is bad. I highly suggest installing a few mods to fix the gameplay and worldbuilding before playing this. If you enjoyed playing this, that's perfectly okay. I just think the base/vanilla game doesn't meet the standards for what a good game is, especially a good Fallout game.

Bethesda revives the Fallout franchise originally produced by Black Isle, and does a pretty damn good job.

Unlike the previous installments, the game is played entirely in real-time and can be switched between first person or third person mode.

The damage and damage reduction system is simplified compared to earlier Fallout games. It works, but armor doesn't feel as effective, especially at high levels.

There is so much content; every time I play, I find new random encounters or npc scavengers in out of the way heaps of rubble. And that's without mods (note: the Steam version REQUIRES the "Archive Invalidation" mod found on Nexusmods.com in order to play on modern systems; so far it seems to be a safe site, but don't click on any outgoing links)

The setting (D.C. Wasteland) is where it really shines though. No other game, Fallout or otherwise, has come close to producing the same feel of living in a post nuclear apocalypse.

From what I hear the support for this game sucks because they just bethesda as normal just completely ignore everything their fans say. It basically doesnt work on pc outright without 2 hours of installing mods and bugfixing. HOWEVER, valve carried because steam deck can run anything with minimal crashes.

Combat isn't the worst but it is undeniably vats carried.
Story is mediocre game is basically side quest carried for world building and content (like most bethesda games).
A lot of the choices do affect some things but there are a lot of obvious things that should change based on your choices and don't (fallout nv is supposed to be much better in this regard but I havent played it)
Graphics are good for the time it came out and the atmosphere is incredible, much better than 4 and 76.

I'm gonna end review by saying that the remaster NEEDS the green tint.

If you use VATS a lot and build your character in a way that VATS (pause and select areas to target) is useful, then this is a great game.

If you do not use VATS for shooting, it is a bad game. In my opinion.
Because it is bad as a shooter.

The graphics did not really age well, but now 2026 it is still playable and enjoyable IF you are clear that it is a game from 2009 with older graphics.

If you use VATS for fights, then you can enjoy them.

The real reason I still enjoy this game so much are the stories.
There are a LOT of stories to find in the wastelands and everyone who talks to you has a voice. It is not just walls of text, you can lean back and enjoy all the different voices that tell you stories, ask for help or threaten you.

It is a nice game, but not for everyone.
I like it but even I have to force myself a bit to keep playing because I am missing all the cool features from Fallout 4 :-)

--------------- Update -----------------
After 10-15 hours played after a long time I have to say I am not so impressed anymore.
This makes sense, the game is OLD. 
But it feels like 
- get a mission to go somewhere
- slaughter everything
- talk to some people with mostly interesting stories
- done

It feels boring. Somehow.
Might be me.

You love video game jank, or you don't. It was jank when it came out and it feels even more jank now
But I don't think what makes a video game good is simply how smooth it plays, rather how engaging it is to work around a game's set systems to progress. fo3's combat IS clunky, yet there is a lot of strategy that can make it work for you rather than against you. I appreciate that it doesnt cater to my FPS instincts and makes me think differently.

I find the dated graphics hold up pretty well. It's the most visibly destroyed wasteland of modern fallout in my opinion, it's a very ugly game with barely any color and nearly every inch of the wasteland has been hit by bombs and reduced to rubble. At that point theres no need to render anything very detailed and the fact that it all looks like crap actually heightens the gritty wasteland atmosphere. The gore hasn't aged though and still looks spectacular today, and the bloody mess perk at times makes the game feel like FEAR. 

The story, graphics and gunplay might all be subpar by today's standards. But there's something undeniably dark and hardcore about 3 AND New Vegas, that is somewhat lost in 4 and 76. It's hard to believe this game is almost 20 years old but it can still be as immersive today as it was back then.

Fallout 3: Game of the Year Edition is a landmark open-world RPG that combines freedom, exploration, and player choice in a haunting post-apocalyptic setting. The Game of the Year Edition includes all major DLC expansions, making it the definitive way to experience the Capital Wasteland.

World & Atmosphere

The ruined remains of Washington D.C. feel eerie, lonely, and immersive. Every broken building and radioactive wasteland tells a story.

Strong environmental storytelling
Constant tension from radiation, mutants, and raiders
A memorable, atmospheric soundtrack that reinforces isolation
Gameplay

The game blends first-person shooting with RPG mechanics through the V.A.T.S. system, which slows time and lets you target specific enemy body parts.

V.A.T.S. adds tactical depth to combat
Character builds feel meaningful (speech, hacking, combat styles)
Exploration is highly rewarding with hidden locations and loot
Story & Choices

You begin searching for your father in a world shaped by moral ambiguity. Choices genuinely matter, affecting how factions and characters react to you.

Branching moral decisions (good, evil, or neutral paths)
Multiple ways to solve quests (combat, diplomacy, stealth)
Player freedom is a major strength
DLC Content (Game of the Year Edition)

The included expansions significantly expand the experience:

Operation: Anchorage – Military simulation focused on combat
The Pitt – Dark moral choices in a harsh industrial settlement
Broken Steel – Extends the main story and raises level cap
Point Lookout – Swamp exploration with eerie mysteries
Mothership Zeta – Sci-fi alien abduction storyline
Criticisms
Gunplay feels dated compared to modern shooters
Some quests are repetitive
Character animations and visuals show their age
Final Verdict

Fallout 3: Game of the Year Edition remains a classic RPG experience defined by freedom, atmosphere, and meaningful choices. Despite aging mechanics, its world design and storytelling still hold up impressively.

A wonderful game from an era that no longer exists. An experience that, has truly stuck with me since my teen years. 

Personal nostalgia bias aside, I think this is one of the best games of it's time. This is a true Bethesda game so jank and infuriating bugs do exist. I will not let nostalgia cloud the technical issues we know Bethesda for, and this game is objectively buggy in many places. Even today on modern systems the ending sequence may cause your game to crash (Windows and Linux). But even with that I don't think it takes away from the overall game too much. 

This game took the walking steps from Elder scrolls Oblivion, and started a jog that would eventually end up where we are today. Where the genre is almost over saturated with fallout/elder scrolls type games. And that is because this foundational pillar from the early years is solid. I still believe the game gives a wonderful expression of having to survive in the wasteland ruins. While yes voice acting is rough for NPC's who aren't part of the main story. And things like no aiming retical is just odd. The execution still works, VAT's the slow-mo attack mode is fun to use, especially with the perk where you explode people. I also feel the story is worth playing through, and not just the main story but the side quests as well. This likely is nostalgia speaking but, something about mindlessly seeing who else might pop up in this messed up world. And what trouble or help they may bring is still such a "magical" feeling. citations.review_text:
Bethesda revives the Fallout franchise originally produced by Black Isle, and does a pretty damn good job.

Unlike the previous installments, the game is played entirely in real-time and can be switched between first person or third person mode.

The damage and damage reduction system is simplified compared to earlier Fallout games. It works, but armor doesn't feel as effective, especially at high levels.

There is so much content; every time I play, I find new random encounters or npc scavengers in out of the way heaps of rubble. And that's without mods (note: the Steam version REQUIRES the "Archive Invalidation" mod found on Nexusmods.com in order to play on modern systems; so far it seems to be a safe site, but don't click on any outgoing links)

The setting (D.C. Wasteland) is where it really shines though. No other game, Fallout or otherwise, has come close to producing the same feel of living in a post nuclear apocalypse.

citations.review_text:
Good (and now) old Fallout 3. Not as cool as New Vegas, but not as buggy as well. 
I remember playing this back in 2008 for a first time, before all those DLCs release (I didn't even knew about DLCs until, probably, 2012). Birthday party, first bottle caps stash (I ignored it at the time - this was my very first Fallout), Megaton, travel to Arefu, radscoprions and first mirelurks, Wasteland survival guide, first travel trough D.C. subway (still one of the best experiences), struggling with super-mutants (highest difficulty - simply because I thought I can), days of exploration (Dunwich building, right after "good" ending of Tenpenny Tower quest), Mechanist and AntAgonizer, dozens of interesting places... Damn it was great. I wish I could erase my memory and play it all again.

Yes, it's pretty clunky, it crashes sometimes, the firearms mechanic felt outdated even back in 2008. But still - it a good game. Maybe not the best Fallout out there, but a good game. Oblivion with guns, as people used to say, I hope it will get at least the same treatment as Oblivion has got.

I have nostalgia for this game, but don't purely base your opinion of this game on hate from youtubers and the like - the game certainly has flaws and appears very dated these days (especially the combat) but it's not to be written off as not worth playing.

The main story is rightfully pretty boring and lame. What Bethesda really nailed with this game was the atmosphere. It does feel really cool to explore the wasteland even if it doesn't make all that much sense. There are also a bunch of great side quests.

Despite having played this game for hours on the PS3 back in the day, I managed to get about 100 hours out of replaying it more recently, so I think that if it goes on sale you're getting good value for your money. 

It's also not as unstable as made out to be once you install only a few stability/enhancement mods (which I did the same for New Vegas and that game still manages the occasional crash every 2 hours unlike 3) and Bethesda also finally removed the GFL integration (better late than never I guess).

The DLCs are also pretty good and besides Mothership Zeta being a bit of a slog they're all pretty good and each adds some new kit for you to use and more (albeit smaller) areas and locations for you to explore and plunder.

[h1]An Outdated Classic[/h1]

i can see how when this game initially came off, it was critically adored for being a faithful enough transition from the classic isometric game system to an open world, 3d first person shooter. however, i have to say that the game unfortunately did not age well. the open world, while expansive, is visually bland with the game suffering from low resolution textures drowned in a green filter. the speed needed to get around is teeth grindingly slow with no way to move faster. the gunplay isn't satisfying and forces you to miss in order to be reliant on the overpowered VATS system.

finally, the game does not run as well as it used to. npcs sometimes bugged out/died randomly (looking at you traders), corpses sometimes disappeared or got stuck in the floor, sounds glitched out or were bass-boosted, animations (rarely admittedly) broke, hell even opening a container was enough to crash to desktop.

i still 100% the game though, as the premise and side-stories were interesting enough, but if i ever choose to revisit this game it would probably be through mods, a potential remaster, or maybe in a video format.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the atmospheric and immersive design of the open world and Washington D.C. wasteland.

citations.review_text:
This game was my first entry into the franchise. There is no better way to start your immersive experience than with Fallout 3. This game gives you a TRUE apocalyptic world where you get to wander through a unnervingly dark environment, discovering the choices that were made by the old world, as you try to survive the new world ahead of you,  as the Lone Wanderer. 

10/10 
If only Fallout 4 wasn't a complete Settlement SIM piece of dog$hit.

To be completely honest, it doesn't quite reach the deep role-playing mechanics of New Vegas. However, it is still far, far better than Fallout 4. The Capital Wasteland itself is a masterclass in atmospheric design. Emerging from Vault 101 into the ruined remains of Washington DC provides a sense of isolation and discovery that is incredibly compelling. I was a good intro for me to the FO universe. 7/10

The first step for the franchise getting a 3D makeover, and it is really beautiful (by wasteland standards). Despite its age, this game is very atmospheric and really feels like a wasteland. The RPG and story might not be the best, especially compared to FO:NV, however it gets the exploration and feel of an actual survival game way better than NV. If you are gonna play this, the Broken Steel DLC/GOTY edition is a MUST buy!

Overall, this is a solid 9/10 for me.
